title: Capacity Ops Slate — Autoscale Editor & Burst Playbook (UX sprint notes)
content:
Purpose
- Capture UX patterns and prototype notes for a single-pane Autoscale Rule Editor + Burst Playbook that operations and SRE teams can use to manage Dedicated GPU pools.
- Provide a usable dry-run / simulation mode so changes can be validated against expected cost and latency impact before committing.

Context / motivation
- Current UX is split across: pool settings, reservations page, and a separate "burst scheduler" hidden in infra. Users want a single place to: view pool utilization, edit autoscale rules (min/max/step), create burst windows (time-bound high-capacity overrides), and run a simulated rollout.
- Primary personas: Platform Ops (owner of Dedicated pool configs), Solutions Eng (customer-facing changes), SRE on-call (quick adjustments during incidents).

High-level goals
- Make autoscale rules discoverable and testable.
- Reduce accidental over-provisioning by surfacing predicted cost vs latency tradeoffs.
- Support temporal bursts with automatic rollback and audit trail.
- Enable safe canary rollouts of policy changes across pools.

Key concepts to represent in UI
- Pool selector (multi-select) with health badges (green/amber/red), regional tag, and commit history link.
- Autoscale rule editor: triggers (utilization, queue length, p95 latency), scale step, cool-down, maintainers.
- Burst playbook: one-off or recurring windows, capacity caps (absolute GPU count or % of pool), emergency-only toggle, notification hooks.
- Timeline/scrubber: shows historical utilization and simulated future when rule applied.
- Dry-run panel: shows predicted token throughput, p95 latency band, estimated hourly cost delta, and risk score (0-10).
- Versioned changes + preview diff and rollback.

Rough wireframe (ASCII sketch for dev/product discussion)
-----------------------------------------------------
| Top bar: [Pool dropdown] [Environment switcher] [Search] |
-----------------------------------------------------
| Left column (20%): pools list  | Center (55%): Timeline + Editor | Right (25%): Details & Dry-run |
| - pool row: name • region • health • active rule tag | - timeline: stacked area: CPU/queue/requests | - rule summary: name, id, author |
| - quick actions: view history / open policy | - timeline scrubber with play/pause | - dry-run results: cost delta / latency impact |
-----------------------------------------------------
| Bottom: audit trail / activity feed + commit controls (Save draft / Run dry-run / Commit / Schedule) |
-----------------------------------------------------

Editor interaction flow (user story)
1) Platform Ops selects "us-west-2 G4-pool" and clicks "Edit autoscale".
2) UI pre-fills rule from last committed version; shows a small diff panel if there are pending drafts.
3) User changes trigger: queue_length > 30 AND p95_latency > 1200ms, scale_step +2 gpus, cooldown 3m.
4) User opens "Burst playbook" tab, schedules a 3-hour burst for 2026-03-20 09:00-12:00 (recurring weekly MWF). Sets cap to +40% or +8 GPUs (user can toggle absolute vs %).
5) User clicks "Run dry-run". The timeline animates, showing a simulated bump in capacity during the scheduled window and overlays predicted p95 and cost curves.
6) Dry-run panel flags a 27% cost increase and warns: "Predicted p95 still above SLO for peak slices — consider larger step or caching."
7) User saves draft, optionally attaches a playbook note and triggers a canary to specified sub-pools.

Dry-run outputs (what we need to compute / expose)
- Predicted cost delta: hourly, 24h, 7d.
- Predicted p95 latency band: baseline vs projected.
- Token throughput capacity change.
- Estimated GPU-hours added and associated dollar cost.
- Risk indicators: policy overlap (two burst windows overlapping), quota exceed warnings, cross-pool conflicts.

Bursts: design notes
- Two modes: Planned (scheduled, visible in calendar) vs Emergency (manual toggle with audit-only retention if not escalated).
- Recurring patterns should be editable as a single rule. UI will show derived instances on the timeline.
- Bursts should optionally create short-lived reservations (API persists under reservations DB) so infra can pre-warm VMs and allocate KV cache priming.
- Each burst gets an "autofallback" policy: if latency < threshold for X minutes, end early.

Backlog / grooming items (rough priority)
- INF-8421: Autoscale Rule Editor skeleton + pool selector (MVP).
- INF-8570: Dry-run simulation engine API contract + UI hooks.
- INF-8612: Burst calendar UI + recurrence editor.
- INF-8649: Reservation-on-burst plumbing (backend) + telemetry for pre-warm success.
- INF-8715: Canary rollout flow for policy changes (subset of pools).
- UX-122: Empty state and onboarding hints for first-time pool editors.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- User can select a pool and edit min/max/step/cooldown and save as draft.
- Dry-run returns a simulated cost delta and renders a timeline overlay.
- User can schedule a one-off burst and see it reflected in timeline preview.
- All edits generate an audit entry with author, timestamp, and diff.

Open questions / decisions
- Should dry-run use exact billing rates or a simplified estimator? (cost team input required)
- How to represent multi-metric triggers elegantly without cognitive overload? (combo builder vs YAML)
- Expose an "autosuggest" for scale_step based on historical scale events? (ML suggestion)
- Defaults for burst caps — absolute GPUs vs percent-of-pool — which is primary?
- How to tie bursts to reservations without requiring manual ticketing?

Edge cases & constraints
- Pools shared across customers (in Dedicated) must not allow cross-tenant bursts. Add guardrails and a customer visibility toggle.
- Calendar recurrence conflicts: show conflict resolution modal if two recurring bursts overlap.
- Offline / degraded infra: allow users to save draft but block commits with explicit warning.

Telemetry / instrumentation needs
- Events: autoscale_rule.view, autoscale_rule.edit, burst.schedule, burst.execute, dryrun.run, policy.commit.
- Metrics to collect: predicted_cost_delta, commit_success, rollback_rate, canary_failure_rate.

Implementation notes for engineers
- Frontend: React + typescript. Timeline uses existing charts lib (re-use capacity heatmap component), but timeline needs time-scrubbing + overlay of simulated capacity.
- Backend: dry-run should be an idempotent endpoint that accepts: pool_id, rule_payload, window_start, window_end, historical_window (optional) and returns cost/latency projection.
- Reservation creation should be a separate API call made only when commit confirms "Create reservation on burst" to avoid unnecessary quotas.

Next actions (owner: Aisha)
- Sprint grooming meeting: 2026-03-09 with infra and cost team to lock cost estimator (assign INF-8570).
- Quick prototype of timeline + dry-run overlay by Marco (due 2026-03-18).
- Draft copy for product microcopy (button labels, warnings) — Sofia to produce v0.
- Coordinate backend contract with backend eng (Daniel) and attach to INF-8421.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the default view low-surface: show only min/max/step and a "advanced" toggle for complex triggers. Ops love single-click actions during incidents.
- Consider keyboard shortcuts for commit / cancel during war room.
- Audit trail should be filterable by pool / actor / date.

References & inspiration
- Link to existing pool UI: /shared_drives/engineering/console-and-tooling/gpu-pool-management-ux-grooming-notes.json
- Calendar recurrence UX inspired by Calendar's recurrence editor and Cloud provider scheduled-scaling flows.

-- end of notes --

(rough — will iterate after sprint grooming)
